fun_facts: At Belleville High School, Bryce Underwood threw for 3,165 yards and 40 touchdowns as a junior, with just two interceptions.
Bryce Underwood's high school team went 50–4, won two state championships, and put together a 38-game winning streak.
Bryce Underwood once kept throwing passes at Michigan's indoor practice field until 2 a.m.; coach Sherrone Moore sent him out to get some sleep.
Bryce Underwood became just the fourth true freshman in Michigan history to start at quarterback.
In 2026, Bryce Underwood threw the game-winning two-point conversion in a triple-overtime win over UCLA.
